newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rejects U.S. criticism of libel award.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rejects U.S. criticism of libel award.

text.p: Singapore brusquely rejected on Friday mild U.S. criticism of record libel damages awarded to ruling party leaders against an opposition politician who called them liars.

"Recourse to legal action against libel and defamation is a democratic and conclusive way to settle disputes, and thus maintain high standards of truth and honesty in politics," the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.

"The other way is to exchange defamation for defamation in the media, with the people never the wiser as to who was lying," it said in reaction to a State Department comment on the award against opposition politician Tang Liang Hong on Thursday. The U.S. criticism of the Singapore $8.08 million (US$5.65 million) damages awarded to Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and 10 colleagues in the ruling People's Action Party (PAP), was muted.
The State Department said it did not have "any particular comment" on the award.

But spokesman John Dinger said the State Department's 1996 human rights report "is critical of the fact that in Singapore government leaders sometimes use defamation suits or the threat of such actions to discourage public criticism".

The Foreign Ministry statement took strong issue with that. "The Singapore Government has consistently and repeatedly pointed out to the State Department our strong disagreement with that view," it said.
"Libel and defamation are taken seriously in Singapore, especially where it concerns the integrity of political leaders or key institutions," it said.
"Failure to rebut such libel or defamation will undermine respect for and credibility of leaders and institutions," it added.

Singapore Justice Chao Hick Tin said on Thursday Goh and his colleagues were justified in calling Tang "an anti-English education, anti-Christian Chinese chauvinist" who was a danger to Singapore's racial harmony.

Tang had made "malicious" attacks on Goh, former prime minister Lee Kuan Yew and the others which could have affected "their moral authority to govern", including calling them liars over the chauvinism charge, Chao said in his judgment.
Tang fled Singapore in January after losing a fierce general election battle in which the PAP won 81 of the 83 seats at stake.
Last week, a Singapore court issued an arrest warrant for Tang to face 33 counts of tax evasion.
